Senses.Explanation: An instant is a very short interval. Yongzheng Emperor says that it is swift as a finger-snap. Wuyi Yuanlai compares three elapsed years to the interval of an instant, while Zhongfeng Mingben says there is no instant without birth and change or cessation. Yongming Yanshou uses flowing water to describe the previous instant ceasing and the next arising. Chijue Daochong gives a finer inherited reckoning whose source-visible count reads literally ‘six-thousand-five’ instants in one finger-snap, followed by 900 arisings and cessations in one instant; no parallel or apparatus variant resolves whether the first written number is meant as 6,005, a colloquially shortened 6,500, or a textual error. Lingao Benyu instead begins from one thought containing ninety instants and likewise gives 900 arisings and cessations within each instant. Those differently framed calculations confirm extreme brevity but do not establish a single modern duration. Yang Jie says the Source-Mirror's treasure is gained without even an instant's exertion. Ziyang Zhenren contrasts becoming buddha in an instant with wandering for myriad ages. These named speakers repeatedly bend the tiny time-unit into a sharp interval for change, attainment, or contrast, without turning the interval into a person, title, or separate lexical object.
